summary: Source-anchored research for Collation and index sort compatibility. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Collation-aware index keys may be larger than keys for indexes without collation because MongoDB uses ICU collation keys to establish string order. (high confidence)

A case-insensitive sort can apply a locale collation to the find operation and then sort by the string field. A case-insensitive index can support that order when the operation uses the same collation; strength 1 or 2 can configure a case-insensitive collation. (medium confidence)

To use an index for string comparisons, an operation must specify the same collation as the index. If an operation specifies a different collation than the index, the index cannot support string comparisons on the indexed fields. Operations on a collection use the collection's default collation unless they explicitly specify a different collation, so check both the collection default and any per-operation override when explaining why MongoDB does not choose a collated index. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createCollection/

MongoDB Jira SERVER-136628 reports that, on a collated collection, pushing a string equality filter into a full index scan used only for sorting can drop matching documents. Its reproducer reports no results instead of two case variants when pushdown is enabled on a local 2026-09-17 build; the ticket was marked Unresolved / Needs Scheduling at its last update on 2026-10-08. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-08)

Matching collations do not remove compound-index sort constraints. Sort fields must appear in index order, their directions must match the index pattern or its full reverse, and a non-prefix sort needs equality predicates on all preceding index fields. Otherwise MongoDB may need a blocking sort. (high confidence)

A collation mismatch does not make every use of a compound index unavailable. For a compound index where the index prefix keys are not strings, arrays, or embedded documents, an operation that specifies a different collation can still use the index to support comparisons on the index prefix keys. In MongoDB's example, a compound index on { year: 1, metacritic: 1, title: 1 } with French ("fr") collation can be used by simple-collation queries that filter on year and sort by title, but a query that also matches on the string field title with simple collation can use the index only for the year portion. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex/
